'''Andrea Naccari''' (12 August 1841 &ndash; 2 October 1919) was an Italian chemist notable for his study of  the [[thermoelectric]] properties of metals, the [[photoelectric effect]] of metals immersed in liquids, and the [[electrical conductivity]] of gases and [[liquid dielectric]]s. He showed that the variation in the [[electrical resistance]] of distilled water was due largely to the solubility of the glass of the receptacle in which it was contained.

He obtained his PhD in pure maths in 1862 at the [[University of Padua]] under [[Francesco Rossetti]].

* ''Atti della R. Accad. delle Scienze di Torino'' 1927, '''63''', pp.&nbsp;24&ndash;30.
